arc: hook (typed caption blows up) → problem ×6 (desk phone, smartphone, video phone ring with 'To book a job' / 'To schedule a meeting' / 'But nobody's around to pickup' between, all joined by pixel-block wipes) → turn ('Until now.' on orange, iris) → reveal (voice orb) → conversation (AI receptionist chat) → benefit ('Stop missing calls…') → feature lineup (three agent cards) → logo

scenes.title: Typed caption blows up into a scattered paper collage, 3D phone dithers in
scenes.summary: On warm off-white grid paper (#efeeea), 'Someone's calling' types out small with a blinking caret, then the two words scale from 30px to 96px and fly apart into a scattered headline while the camera starts a slow leftward drift. The sentence finishes as 'to make an appointment.' with words and grey object tiles (spray can, pipette, scissors, hair dryer), an orange headset app icon and a black handset glyph popping in hard. In the last 22 frames a real 3D desk phone on a blue halftone field switches on cell by cell over the paper, leaning in, and a glass 'INCOMING CALL' pill pops up.
scenes.build: Typing is a plain slice of the string by frame; the grow is one inOutCubic interpolate lerping font size and two word positions. PaperCamera (components/PaperBeats.tsx) puts content on a 2×-wide Paper world and translates it left linearly; AppointmentProps uses ScatterWords/Pop/IconTile/DitherTile (Scatter.tsx, Tile.tsx) for 4-frame hard pop entrances. PhoneStage (PhoneStage.tsx) is one ThreeScene canvas holding a GLSL dither-gradient quad plus a base64-packed phone mesh; its 'cover' wipe uploads a 24×14 DataTexture mask each frame and discards fragments per cell so the DOM paper shows through.
scenes.reuse: Borrow the caption-to-headline blow-up and the hard-pop object collage for any 'everyday pain' opener; swap the words, the lucide icons in the tiles and the accent colours. The PhoneStage wipe is the trick worth studying for any WebGL surface that must pixel-wipe over DOM. Don't copy the 2.5MB phone mesh JSON unless you need a phone; the salon icon set is template-specific.

scenes.title: 3D desk phone rings on a halftone field, pixel-wipes away to 'To book a job.'
scenes.summary: A textured 3D corded desk phone buzzes and bobs on a blue-to-olive dithered halftone gradient with the 'INCOMING CALL' glass pill floating at top right. In the last 18 frames the phone leans back and the whole surface breaks away in ragged square cells sweeping right-to-left, revealing the paper beneath where 'To book a job.', a blue 'book' button and a cursor start popping in.
scenes.build: PhoneStage in 'reveal' wipe mode (cells discard as they switch on) with leanOut() tilt from Phone3D.tsx; timeOffset carries the previous scene's drift so the cut is invisible. The paper underneath is plain DOM (Paper + BookJobPaper started LEAD frames early). IncomingPill is a DOM glass pill with an until-fade.
scenes.reuse: Use as a reference for a WebGL object scene that exits via an in-shader block wipe into a DOM scene. Swap the mesh, the gradient stops in FIELD_FRAG and the pill copy. Mostly meaningful paired with its neighbours.

scenes.title: 'To book a job.' trades collage drifts, smartphone blocks in
scenes.summary: The paper keeps drifting left past 'To book a job.' with trade objects (tape measure, hard hat, traffic cone, hi-vis vest, crane) and the already-clicked blue 'book' button. In the last 18 frames a blue halftone field with a tilted smartphone (pulsing green answer button) and an 'INCOMING CALL' pill blocks in from the right.
scenes.build: PaperCamera with BookJobPaper offset by CARRY=30 frames (the beat began in scene 02); overlay is a DOM BlockReveal (components/BlockReveal.tsx) wrapping IncomingField + SmartPhone from Devices.tsx — BlockReveal merges lit cells into overflow-hidden runs, each holding a copy of the children, instead of clip-path.
scenes.reuse: Only as the tail of the book-a-job beat; the real work is in PaperBeats.tsx and BlockReveal.tsx. Near-duplicate of scenes 05 and 07 in structure.

scenes.title: CSS smartphone rings on dither, blocks out to 'To schedule a meeting.'
scenes.summary: A tilted black smartphone shakes on the blue halftone field, green answer button pulsing, 'INCOMING CALL' pill above. After 27 frames the paper with 'To schedule a meeting.' and a dark green 'Meeting · Today 10:00 AM' calendar card blocks in over it cell by cell.
scenes.build: DOM-only: IncomingField (Dither.tsx halftone via mask-image dot grid over drifting radial gradients) + SmartPhone, then BlockReveal in reveal mode over Paper + MeetingPaper. Frame offsets (PREV_LEN) keep the shake and drift continuous with scene 03.
scenes.reuse: Shows the DOM version of the block wipe; same pattern as scenes 02/06. Swap device/copy. Little to learn beyond BlockReveal itself.

scenes.title: 'To schedule a meeting.' office collage, 3D video phone switches on
scenes.summary: Paper drifts past 'To schedule a meeting.' with the Meeting card (toggle already on), laptop, pencil, mug, keyboard, notebook, armchair and calendar tiles. In the last 18 frames a 3D video desk phone with a glowing screen covers the paper cell by cell, leaning in, and the 'INCOMING CALL' pill pops at top right.
scenes.build: PaperCamera + MeetingPaper offset by CARRY; PhoneStage with videoMesh, model='video', 'cover' wipe and leanIn() tilt. Identical structure to scene 01's tail.
scenes.reuse: Near-duplicate of 01/03's pattern with a different object set; borrow 01 instead.

scenes.title: 3D video phone rings, pixel-wipes to 'But nobody's around…'
scenes.summary: The 3D video desk phone buzzes on the halftone field with the 'INCOMING CALL' pill, then leans back and discards itself cell by cell to reveal the paper where 'But nobody's around to pickup.' begins popping in among objects from all three worlds.
scenes.build: Same as scene 02: PhoneStage reveal wipe with videoMesh, leanOut tilt, timeOffset continuity; NobodyPaper underneath as DOM.
scenes.reuse: Near-duplicate of scene 02 with a different mesh; study 02 or PhoneStage.tsx instead.

scenes.title: 'But nobody's around to pickup.' collage breaks into an orange flood
scenes.summary: The paper drifts past the scattered headline 'But nobody's around to pickup.' surrounded by a dense collage of a dozen object tiles (hat, cone, mug, keyboard, calendar, scissors, laptop…). Over the last 24 frames a red→orange gradient field with a warm bloom and small dithered blocks along the bottom floods in through ragged pixel blocks, ending fully orange.
scenes.build: PaperCamera + NobodyPaper (CARRY offset) with a BlockReveal overlay whose children are OrangeField (OrangeField.tsx: animated radial bloom over a linear gradient, 14 seeded Dither blocks skylining the bottom).
scenes.reuse: Good pattern for ending a problem section by flooding to a brand colour before a turn. Swap the copy, objects and the OrangeField gradient.

scenes.title: 'Until now.' on orange, irises down to a glowing disc
scenes.summary: White 'Until now.' fades in word by word, centred on the drifting orange field. The words fade out and the whole frame irises down (inOutCubic) from full screen to a 440px orange disc on black, while a dim green/amber halo and three thin concentric rings bloom around it.
scenes.build: A radial-gradient mask-image whose hard edge radius is interpolated from 1500px to 220px clips the OrangeField; TextAnimation by='word' preset='fadeIn' with an exit. Rings (Orb.tsx) are bordered circles whose diameter and opacity stagger in. The disc lands exactly where scene 09's orb starts.
scenes.reuse: Great 'until now' / 'what if' pivot: swap the line and colours; the iris-to-disc handoff works for any reveal of a circular logo or product. Keep the disc size matched to the next scene.

scenes.title: Flat disc ignites into a breathing voice orb, shrinks to an avatar
scenes.summary: The flat orange disc heats into a luminous orb (white-hot core sliding through yellow to red, soft glow) inside thin rings on black, breathing gently. In the last 30 frames it shrinks from 440px to a 44px avatar and travels up-left while a blurred green mesh-gradient world fades up behind it.
scenes.build: Orb (Orb.tsx) layers a flat radial disc under a 'hot' radial gradient whose highlight point orbits with sin/cos; `heat` cross-fades them and glow is a breathing box-shadow. Size/position lerp to the AVATAR slot used by scene 10. Mesh.tsx is six drifting radial-gradient blobs.
scenes.reuse: Borrow the CSS orb for any voice/AI-assistant reveal; recolour the gradient stops. The shrink-to-avatar move is a clean bridge into a chat UI.

scenes.title: AI receptionist chat: glass bubbles type out over a blurred mesh
scenes.summary: On a drifting green mesh gradient, three frosted glass bubbles appear and type themselves out in step with voiceover: 'Reception': 'Hi there. How can I help you today?', 'You': 'Hey, I'm looking to book an appointment for next week, please?' (right side), then 'Reception': 'Sure! When would be a good time for you?'. Small glowing orb avatars mark the agent lines. The scene ends by blurring and dimming to black.
scenes.build: A local Bubble component: entrance via translateY/scale ease, typed text sliced at ~0.66 chars/frame to match the VO, and a hidden full-text span reserving the box so the bubble never reflows. Bubbles are timed by `at` frames (0, 68, 172) matching voiceover clips in project.json. Mesh + Orb components for backdrop and avatars.
scenes.reuse: Strong template for any AI-agent or support-chat demo: swap speaker names, lines, `at` timings (sync to your VO) and the backdrop. The reserved-box typing trick is worth copying verbatim.

scenes.title: Benefit line in an outline frame that collapses into a gradient card
scenes.summary: On black, 'Stop missing calls and opportunities' fades in word by word inside a thin rounded white outline frame that nearly fills the screen. The words blur away and the outline collapses (inOutCubic) to a 540×300 card in the centre, which fills with a green mesh-gradient 'Receptionist agent' card face.
scenes.build: Outline div with left/top/width/height/radius all lerped from a full-frame rect to CENTER_CARD (AgentCard.tsx); the AgentCard fades in over the last 14 frames with textOpacity 0. TextAnimation word fadeIn with hold='breathe' and an exit.
scenes.reuse: Use to turn a tagline into the first product card of a lineup; swap copy and gradient. The geometry handoff only makes sense with scene 12.

scenes.title: Three mesh-gradient agent cards fan out, then squash into one bar
scenes.summary: The centre 'Receptionist agent — Full appointment booking system' card is joined by 'Informational agent — Answer questions, no booking needed' and 'Reservation agent — Bookings for spaces and equipment' sliding out from behind it; each has a lucide icon in a glass square over a teal/green/yellow mesh gradient and floats gently. The copy fades, then all three squash (inOutCubic) into one 28px-high, full-width three-segment gradient bar.
scenes.build: Data array of three cards; each card's left/top/width/height/radius is lerped from its spread slot to its third of BAR, with `spread` and `squash` interpolates. AgentCard.tsx draws the gradient face, scrim, icon tile and two text lines.
scenes.reuse: Great for 'three products / plans / agent types' and as a bridge into a logo: swap titles, subs, icons and gradients; the squash-into-bar handoff pairs with scene 13. Card count is a one-line change.

scenes.title: Gradient bar thins away into a blur-in 'Reception.ai' wordmark
scenes.summary: The three-segment gradient bar thins to a hairline and fades, a soft pool of light breathes in, and 'Reception' (white) '.ai' (muted grey) blurs in character by character at 96px. Under it an ElevenLabs mark + 'ElevenLabs Agents' credit slides up, holds, and fades before the end.
scenes.build: Bar height interpolated to 1px; TextAnimation by='char' preset='blurIn' with exit='auto' for the two wordmark halves; the credit line uses Img with the SVG asset and an in/out opacity interpolate.
scenes.reuse: Clean, minimal wordmark resolve for any dark close; swap the two text halves and the 'powered by' credit. Don't ship the ElevenLabs logo/name for another brand.
